title: Inference Attributor: unified decomposition service for per-route/model/customer metrics
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a centralized Attribution Engine (the 'Attributor') that produces deterministic, explainable breakdowns of token-level cost and latency per route, model variant, and customer. This service will combine streaming per-request events (ingest) with batch reconciliations to emit daily and real-time attribution slices used by Console dashboards, billing rollups, and SLO analyses. The Attributor must account for KV cache hits/misses, model fallback routing, batching amplifications, and GPU kernel-level weighted token cost. Outputs must be queryable by route, model, customer, time-window and include confidence metadata for sampled data.
acceptance_criteria: Service exposes gRPC ingestion API and batch job interface; integration tests simulate 10k req/s with sampling
Outputs materialize per-tenant daily slices with fields: route_id, model_family, model_variant, customer_id, token_count, usd_cost, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, attribution_version
Console dashboard consumes attribution slices via read API and shows per-route cost breakdown matched within 1% to billing rollups for sample dataset
Backfill completes for last 90 days without >3% delta against existing heuristics and finishes within SLA window
End-to-end trace: for a given request id, can walk attribution chain (cache hit, batched, fallback) and reconcile to slice entries
technical_notes: Design: two-stage pipeline: (1) streaming pre-aggregator that computes per-second micro-slices, enriched with KV cache tag and kernel-time estimates; (2) deterministic reconciler (batch) that merges micro-slices into stable daily attribution using idempotent keys
Cost model: use configurable model profiles per model_variant with per-token weight and per-op kernel multipliers; store profiles in redis+git-backed config for atomic rollouts

Latency decomposition: attribute observed tail to components (proxy_ms, runtime_queue_ms, kernel_exec_ms, network_ms). Use latency histograms with reservoir sampling for tail percentiles to limit cardinality
Sampling: adopt deterministic reservoir sampling keyed by customer_id to ensure reproducible sampled attributions for SLOs
Storage: per-day Parquet partitions in data lake with companion materialized MV in ClickHouse for real-time UI queries; maintain provenance log in Postgres for reconciliation
Rollouts: feature-flag attribution_version to enable safe switch and canary on subset of tenants
Operational: add SLOs for staleness (republish <5m for near-real-time lanes, daily batch <30m), and alerting for data drift vs. expected token rates
tasks: proto/gRPC schema for ingestion + example client
implement streaming pre-aggregator (go) with local KV tagger
implement deterministic batch reconciler (spark or flink) with join to model profiles
schema migration: create Parquet partition layout + ClickHouse MV
write integration tests that replay synthetic request traces with cache/hit patterns

risks_mitigations: Risk: cardinality explosion for route+model+customer — Mitigation: use deterministic bucketing for low-traffic routes and roll up to 'other' after threshold
Risk: model profile inaccuracies cause billing mismatch — Mitigation: add reconciliation job that computes delta vs billing-ledger daily and flags >1% deltas
Risk: sampling induces SLO blindspots — Mitigation: deterministic sampling + targeted full-trace runs for top-50 tenants
owner_notes: Focus first on deterministic correctness + explainability; optimize for cost after core invariants hold. Aim for a conservative attribution_version rollout with canary on 5% tenants by 2026-03-25.
